title: Forms of government
competency: Identify monarchy, aristocracy, dictatorship and democracy.

keywords.def: Rule by one person, a king or queen, who inherits the right to rule.
Rule by a small class of people thought to be best qualified to rule.
Rule by one person or a small group with unlimited power, kept by force.
A form of government in which the rulers are chosen by the citizens.

en.text: We classify governments by how many people hold sovereign power. In a monarchy one person, a king or queen, inherits the right to rule. In an aristocracy a small class thought best qualified rules. In a dictatorship one person or a small group holds unlimited power by force. In a democracy the citizens choose their rulers in free elections.

screens.title: Who rules next?
screens.ask: In one country, the king's eldest son becomes the next king. What do we call this form of government?
screens.after: Rule by a king or queen who inherits power is a monarchy. Read on for the other forms.

screens.title: 2.4 Forms of government
paras: Here we classify them by how many people hold sovereign power.

screens.title: I. Monarchy and II. Aristocracy
paras: Monarchy: sovereign power is in one person, the monarch, with a hereditary right to rule.
The monarch may be a king or queen. The throne usually passes to the eldest son.
Aristocracy: power is in a class of people thought to be superior and best qualified.
Power is in the hands of a few, but it is meant to serve the many.

screens.title: III. Dictatorship and IV. Democracy
paras: Dictatorship: one person or a small group holds unlimited power. Force keeps them in power.
Democracy: the rulers are chosen by the citizens.
It fosters equality, so everyone has an equal chance to develop.
Free and open elections are held. Citizens have a voice through elected officials.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Rule by one person, a king or queen, who inherits the right to rule.
Rule by a small class of people thought to be best qualified to rule.
Rule by one person or a small group with unlimited power, kept by force.
A form of government in which the rulers are chosen by the citizens.

screens.text: What do we use here to classify forms of government?
opts: The number of people holding sovereign power
screens.ans: The number of people holding sovereign power
screens.why: The book classifies forms by how many people hold sovereign power.

pairs: A king or queen inherits power
screens.why: Each form has its own way of holding power.
screens.clue: Think of who rules and how they got power.

screens.text: In a democracy, free and open elections are held.
screens.why: All true democracies hold free and open elections.
screens.clue: Look at the ballot box in Figure 2.10.

screens.text: Ethiopia was ruled for centuries by emperors who inherited the throne. What form was that?
screens.why: Emperors inherited the throne: that is monarchy.
screens.clue: Who held power, and how did they get it?

screens.text: A leader takes power with the army, bans elections and allows no one to question him. Which form is this?
screens.why: Unlimited power kept by force, without elections, is a dictatorship. He did not inherit the throne, so it is not a monarchy.
screens.clue: Did he inherit power, or take it by force?

items.text: Which country still has a monarchy?
items.why: The United Kingdom has a king. Ethiopia's monarchy ended in 1974.
items.clue: Which country has a king today?

items.text: What was Ethiopia's government for many centuries?
opts: A monarchy of kings and emperors
items.ans: A monarchy of kings and emperors
items.why: Emperors such as Menelik II and Haile Selassie I ruled; the monarchy ended in 1974.

test.text: In which form of government do citizens choose their rulers?
test.why: In a democracy the rulers are chosen by the citizens.

test.text: In a monarchy, the throne usually passes to the eldest son.
test.why: The book says the throne usually passes to the eldest son or closest male descendant.

test.text: Which form uses force to keep unlimited power?
test.why: Force is used to keep power in a dictatorship.
